title: Persistent recent chats and a quieter Orbit
highlights: Orbit keeps your two most recent non-archived chats per account available while idle. Clicking opens the exact chat in that account’s Desktop app.
Desktop launches directly without a project-folder picker or opening a project. VS Code keeps its open-window shortcuts.
Idle avatars are still. A small status dot replaces continuous plush animation, and attention reminders use a simple static badge.

title: Orbit sessions and reliable updates
highlights: The desktop launcher owns Orbit for Desktop, CLI and VS Code. Open editor windows stay visible on New Chat and navigate to their owning window.
Hyprland gets a fixed layer overlay; native GNOME, Plasma and Mac checks cover visibility, fullscreen and close-to-tray behavior.
Mini avatars show multiple chats, inactive accounts stay dim, and Stable or All updates follow the same website classification.
Wider Settings use two columns on larger windows. What’s New includes every release since your previous version, grouped by version.

title: Orbit, Orbiters and reliable shared chats
highlights: Orbiters bring live Codex Desktop sessions, usage and quiet reminders into an optional desktop strip.
Turn Orbit off in Settings; adjust its companions and reopen minimal update notes from the version label.
Shared chats retain complete history and attachment paths with reliable settings, archive actions and account handoff.

title: Accurate disk usage and simpler storage settings
highlights: Storage counts unique allocated files, shows honest GiB units and excludes active accounts from clearable cache.
Compact account rows keep detailed recovery and shared-chat controls under expandable sections.
Verified account launches reuse pinned shared packages; failed publications clear temporary staging.

title: Self-contained AppImage helper libraries
highlights: Bundled WebKit helper programs inherit the AppImage library directories, so startup works without system WebKit installed.
Release checks remove system WebKit before testing offline startup; Mac scripts retain /Applications/Multi Codex.app.

title: AppImage startup and system-wide Mac installation
highlights: Linux AppImages locate bundled WebKit helper executables correctly when launched from other folders.
Mac install and update scripts use /Applications/Multi Codex.app while preserving account and conversation data.

title: Quiet automatic update discovery
highlights: Checks for updates quietly at startup, on account refresh, when returning to the app and when reconnecting.
The Update button appears when a newer release is available, with signed installation, progress and automatic restart.

title: Local chat cleanup and one-click updates
highlights: Inspect account storage by category and preview deletion of all local chats or chats last active more than 30 days ago.
The Update button downloads signed packages, shows progress and installs the latest launcher with a clear restart state.
Detailed release notes now live on the website, with GitHub providing package downloads and a short link.

title: Windows credential and installer fixes
highlights: Full-sized Windows logins now save in Credential Manager while keeping existing accounts readable.
PowerShell installation and updates correctly verify GitHub checksum downloads; the direct Windows installer remains available.

title: Windows support and reliable account switching
highlights: Native Windows x64 launcher and extension packages add private account storage, isolated launches and verified install/update scripts.
Mac account menus, all-account usage refresh, connection recovery, long-chat support and persistent Hyprland maximization improve everyday use.

title: Launch settings and terminal picker improvements
highlights: A cleaner terminal picker shows Automatic and installed terminals, with keyboard navigation and a checkmark for your selection.
Workspace and Launching have their own settings sections. Save and Cancel stay visible while advanced options scroll.

title: Terminal preferences and usage reset reminders
highlights: Choose your preferred CLI terminal in Launch settings, including Kitty, Ghostty and the platform’s native terminals.
Grouped reminders show available resets expiring within 48 hours, at most twice a day and at least four hours apart.
The Orange theme preview now matches dark mode.

title: CLI launches for saved accounts
highlights: Launch the Codex CLI from an account row, using that account’s isolated home and your chosen project folder.
Usage refreshes at startup, accounts follow plan order, and six color palettes work in light and dark mode.

title: Desktop launch options and first-run setup
highlights: Launch an account in VS Code, the supported Codex desktop app, or both, with separate account credentials and desktop state.
A first-run welcome detects installed apps, and Launch settings adds a preferred folder with a built-in Browse picker.

title: Workspace folder picker
highlights: A built-in workspace folder browser opens over the app and passes your selection to the existing desktop chooser.

title: Hyprland window sizing fix
highlights: The main app opens full-screen on Hyprland, while folder and desktop selection remain compact dialogs.

title: Hyprland desktop selection and storage controls
highlights: On Hyprland, choose the current desktop or desktops 1–10 for a newly launched VS Code window.
Inspect storage by account and safely clear reclaimable caches while keeping credentials, conversations and settings.

title: Documentation and screenshot updates
highlights: Updated interface screenshots show account limits, alongside clearer instructions for updating the app.

title: Repeated launch reliability
highlights: Repeated launches preserve the account’s existing profile while opening another VS Code window.

title: Launch and usage refresh fixes
highlights: Simplified account launches and improved live limit refresh, including clearer handling of expired sessions.

title: Account session isolation fixes
highlights: Credentials, extensions, browser sign-in, workspaces and local history stay isolated so accounts cannot replace one another’s active login.

title: Live account usage limits
highlights: Live account limit windows replace manual usage entry, with remaining percentages and reset times reported by Codex.

title: Linux and macOS installer improvements
highlights: Added Arch Linux and macOS installers, a verified AppImage update script, and corrected desktop launcher icons.

title: Manual account usage tracking
highlights: Optional account usage tracking adds a way to record and view usage alongside saved accounts.

title: Linux desktop launcher integration
highlights: AppImage desktop integration adds a launcher entry and icon, with a more polished account interface.

title: Linux package checksum correction
highlights: Corrected the published Linux artifact checksums so downloads can be checked against the release’s actual packages.

title: Initial Linux release
highlights: The first Linux release launches multiple Codex accounts in isolated VS Code windows while preserving your current login.
